Recorded claim:
The feature check collects flags from primary-key self-signatures and user-ID self-signatures, skips revoked user IDs and photo user IDs, then removes Thunderbird-supported flags from the bitmask. The landed supported mask held MDC only; AEAD and v5 bits were defined but unsupported. The code also checks a newly imported key object before the import UI warns. This is a feature-advertisement test, not proof that the key material itself is unusable. Current RNP.sys.mjs retains the same structure.

Provenance: 358b723fe525763b5ba9527378b737cb7f4a0aa4e304388e6175a51569d917f3. Original evidence IDs: 39fdd5d78a50b34ac2c95a46140e54557d1d5fe4846f663115c00bd33c68d539, 3fa872ac2d44c648ddc6e44ae3cda805c9f87d653d40de5636f2cb5b8923bf91, c08d335c70fb9891017128812c5ea80a43c17b961dee21e87cbcdffeb9d58313.
This is a recorded historical interpretation, not independent source verification. Source quotes from personal imports or unconfirmed-access records remain private. Historical test results are reported outcomes; no tests were rerun for this backfill.

title: Recorded lesson: Check self-signatures and live user IDs before deciding a key advertises unsupported features
